Independent reproduction /tmp/opencode/crown-audit.py applied the inequality to adjacency masks, unioned closed neighborhoods, and checked induced reachability for all subsets for n=3..7. Global totals were 16,121,306,2004,4306; the two small polynomials and minimum size/count for n=5,6,7 agreed. No nonglobal or disconnected defensive alliance occurred for n=5..7.
correctness.rationale: With the closed-neighborhood convention the threshold for a selected vertex in the (n−1)-regular crown is ceil((n−2)/2)=q. For a selected vertex the only missing potential selected opposite neighbor is its matched mate, so a doubled index forces both shore sizes at least q+1; otherwise both must be at least q. Because q>=1, nonempty alliances meet both shores. At n>=5, at least two chosen vertices per shore guarantee domination, at most one being nonadjacent to any given outside vertex. For c=0 the induced subgraph is complete bipartite; for c>0 both sizes are at least three, so any two selected vertices on one shore have a common selected neighbor, and every selected vertex has a neighbor. For n=3,4, a singleton selected shore in the disjoint case leaves the opposite matched vertex undominated, so global alliances are exactly sets with at least two selected vertices on each shore. Expanding (sum_{j=2}^n binom(n,j)x^j)^2 gives both claimed boundary polynomials. The four-state multinomial formula has correct weights, and equality at the minimum 2q for n>=5 requires disjoint q-element shore selections, with exactly the stated multiplicity. The comparison with K_{n,n} uses the closed-neighborhood inequality in both graphs.
residual_risks: Finite checks supplement the proof; the n>=5 connectivity statement does not extend to every global defensive alliance at the two smaller orders.

evidence: The indexed feasibility lemma requires disjoint shore selections of sizes at least q or arbitrary selections of sizes at least q+1. It gives the ordinary minimum 2q and the coefficient binom(n,q)binom(n−q,q) in its minimal census. The same lemma applies at n=3,4.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: When q>=2 the lemma immediately gives domination by the at-most-one missing cross neighbor; the disjoint selections induce complete bipartite graphs, and with overlap both sides have size>=3 so the induced graph is connected. Therefore summing the labelled four-state multinomials over the already classified family directly gives the whole global enumerator, including even n. The minimum and its count coincide for the same reason. At q=1, domination excludes just the disjoint selections with a shore of size one, leaving arbitrary selections of size at least two per shore on these two graphs. No extra structural or counting input beyond the indexed criterion and the defining matching is necessary.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: For odd n>=5 the crown degree is even, so the strong and closed-neighborhood defensive inequalities impose the same integer threshold. Connectivity and domination are automatic at that threshold by the indexed feasibility lemma, so the odd-order polynomials and minimum counts coincide. The strong polynomial is not equivalent at even n, where the threshold is one higher.

originality.rationale: The exact all-set defensive feasibility criterion under the same convention already has equivalent indexed coverage. For n>=5 the asserted globality, connectivity, enumerator, minimum and count follow directly from that criterion and the fixed deleted matching; odd-order enumerators are explicitly covered via an equivalent strong-alliance invariant in this regime. The boundary counts add no distinct nonroutine claim. These are statements about available equivalent coverage and implication, not priority inferences from same-day or later displayed dates.
residual_risks: Priority was not determined. The inaccessible graph-construction paper and bounded coverage elsewhere do not affect the conclusion from the inspected exact criterion and direct implication.

value.rationale: The exact structural characterization of a natural graph family would be valuable from scratch. Once the equivalent all-set classification and the odd-order exact polynomial are credited, the remaining counts are the direct multinomial weight sum over known feasible profiles (and the elementary two-shore square at n=3,4). Automatic domination and connectivity follow directly from the known per-shore sizes and a single missing neighbor. No distinct motivated exact result beyond that mechanical specialization survives; the two small expansions or the subtraction from the known complete-bipartite minimum do not rescue it.
residual_risks: This is a judgment of the surviving contribution, not an assertion that exact alliance polynomials are intrinsically without scientific use.
